newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary prosecutor to probe adviser in APV scandal.
newsitem.headline: Hungary prosecutor to probe adviser in APV scandal.

text.p: Hungary's Chief Prosecutor said on Tuesday he had ordered an investigation of the activities of adviser Marta Tocsik who is at the centre of a scandal within the state privatisation agency APV over illegal payments.

The scandal, which has rocked Hungary's political system, prompted Prime Minister Gyula Horn to sack Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman following the dismissal on Friday of the whole of APV's executive board.
Tocsik was commissioned by APV to negotiate with local councils with a view to reducing the amount of assets to be transferred to them following privatisation.
Under a law passed in 1989, local councils must be recompensed for land on which formerly state-owned companies are located.
Controversy surfaced at the end of September surrounding the payment by APV to Tocsik of a huge "success fee" of 804 million forints ($5.2 million), or 10 percent of the money she saved.
On Wednesday Tocsik is due to appear, along with APV managing director Istvan Kocsis, before parliament's Constitutional Committee, which is conducting its own inquiry into the affair.
A record wave of privatisation revenues at the end of last year helped Hungary to fill the gap in its state budget and repay a substantial chunk of its huge foreign state debt.
The prime minister's Office said on Monday the scandal would not affect Hungary's privatisation programme.
